response: Yes, β-catenin has been implicated in the pathogenesis of sebaceous cell carcinoma of the eyelid. Mutations in the CTNNB1 gene, which encodes β-catenin, have been identified in a subset of sebaceous cell carcinomas, leading to abnormal activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. This aberrant activation can contribute to tumorigenesis and tumor progression in sebaceous cell carcinoma of the eyelid.
